name.purpose: The hero name on the home page, set on two lines. The one big voice.

post-title.purpose: The h1 on post pages, one step down because post titles run long.

section-title.purpose: Work, Writing and Contact on the home page. The widest cut on the site.

plate-name.purpose: The product name across the top of a plate.

subhead.purpose: Inner-page section heads such as Role, Stack, Highlights and At a glance.

bench-title.purpose: The More projects heading over the bench.

role-line.purpose: The role under the name in the hero.

lead.purpose: The line under a page title. The hero tagline and the Contact lead use the same size at 1.45.

reading.purpose: Long text in posts, project overviews and the About page, within the 46ch measure.

small.purpose: Footer, list labels, dates and meta lines. Labels at this size go bold, never capitals.

mark.purpose: Hallmark letters, set in capitals. 12px in bench rows. A domain keeps its lowercase at 14px with 0.015em tracking.

button.purpose: Button labels in sentence case. 14px in the masthead CV button.

shadows.name: screen-lift
shadows.purpose: Under a product screen on a steel plate. A filter on the screen wrapper, so it follows the bevel.

shadows.name: screen-lift-contract-lens
shadows.purpose: The same lift on the Contract Lens plate, tinted with its ink.

shadows.name: screen-lift-reema
shadows.purpose: The same lift on the Reema night field.

shadows.name: masthead-rule
shadows.purpose: A 1px Steel Rule line under the sticky masthead. A line, not a lift.

motion.name: ease-strike
motion.purpose: The strike easing: a fast press and a long settle.

motion.name: strike-press
motion.purpose: Each mark dips 2px and scales to 0.86 at 18%, then springs back.

motion.name: strike-flash
motion.purpose: A flash of the mark's own ink (currentColor) rises to 0.62 opacity at 14% and fades.

motion.name: strike-stagger
motion.purpose: Delay between marks in a row, set by each mark's --i index.

motion.name: strike-trigger
motion.purpose: Rows with data-strike get data-struck the first time 40% of the row is in view: the home hero register and every plate's hallmark row.

motion.name: button-face
motion.purpose: Hover darkens the button face. A press moves it down 1px.

motion.name: scroll
motion.purpose: In-page jumps glide and stop 16px below the sticky masthead.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Removes the strike, button transitions and smooth scroll. Marks stay fully drawn.

breakpoints.name: hero-stack
breakpoints.purpose: The hero goes to one column, and the tagline widens to 40ch.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Plates, bench rows, the project grid and the Contact band stack. The large stamp hides. Bench rows pad 22px.

breakpoints.name: phone-capture
breakpoints.purpose: Screens switch to phone captures. Plate screens cap at 380px and bench screens at 280px.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: The masthead name hides. Register, keyed, post and ledger rows stack. Action buttons go full width.

narrative.overview:
The site reads like an assay register. One maker stamps every piece of work with the same SP mark. Each piece carries a row of hallmarks that anyone can check: whether it runs live, where its code is, and the domain where it runs. The maker's own pages are polished steel and ink, and blued steel is the maker's color. Each live product wears its own real colors wherever it appears. The SP mark stays blued on all of them.

Type does most of the work. Science Gothic, a squared grotesque with a width axis, cuts the name, the headings, the marks and the buttons. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next sets every line meant for reading. Marks are flat cartouches with cut corners. A mark is struck solid when the thing it names is built, and pale when it is not built yet. The density is calm: wide bands of color, a 1240px frame, and tight gaps inside each group of marks.

Real product screens and the headshot are the only pictures. The site's own surfaces carry no texture, gradient or glass, no hairline grid, no eyebrow labels and no section numbers. Only a product screen casts a shadow. The work never appears as a grid of same-size project cards or as text-left, image-right feature bands.
keyCharacteristics: Polished steel ground, ink text and one accent, blued steel.
Cut corners on every standalone shape. Nothing is rounded.
Struck capitals in marks that certify facts: SP, Live, Code, dates and layers built.
Live products in their own colors, on full-bleed plates and bench rows.
Science Gothic cut wide or narrow with its width axis, and Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for reading.
One motion, the strike, which presses each mark in turn and never hides it.

rules.name: The Maker's Mark Rule
rules.body: The SP mark is always Blued Steel with Blued Paper letters, on every colorway, page and share card. A product may recolor every other mark but never this one. The Contact band is the one exception: it is blued itself, so its SP stamp turns steel with blued letters.

rules.name: The Own Colors Rule
rules.body: A product's colors stay on that product's plate, bench row, project page header and share card. The maker's pages never borrow them, and no product wears another's.

rules.name: The Legible Colorway Rule
rules.body: A new colorway fills every role in the table from the product's real colors, and every text pair passes 4.5:1. When nothing softer passes on the field, soft text stays at full strength, so the Trading Desk's soft text is white on its teal (4.77:1). Summaries in light text on the teal and night fields get a 1.68 line height and 0.01em tracking.

rules.name: The One Big Voice Rule
rules.body: The name is the largest type on the site, and everything else steps well below it. Nothing outgrows the name's 88px.

rules.name: The Cut Width Rule
rules.body: Science Gothic's width axis sets how wide each heading is cut. Section titles are widest (125), then page titles (120), marks and section heads (118), plate and bench names (116), the name (112), running titles (108-114) and the role line (106). Reading text never uses Science Gothic.

rules.name: The Struck Capitals Rule
rules.body: Capitals belong to marks. Headings, buttons and labels stay in mixed case, and open tracking (0.04em and wider) is for marks only. A domain inside a mark keeps its lowercase.

rules.name: The Full-Bleed Field Rule
rules.body: A colorway's field runs edge to edge. Only the content inside it returns to the 1240px frame.

rules.name: The 44px Rule
rules.body: Every text control is at least 44px tall: nav links, text actions, back links, footer links and the home link. Buttons are 48px, and the masthead CV button is 40px.

rules.name: The Lifted Proof Rule
rules.body: Only a real product screen on a plate casts a shadow. Everything else stays flat, and nothing gets a hard offset shadow.

rules.name: The Cut Corner Rule
rules.body: If an object stands alone, cut its corners with a bevel sized to it. If it sits in text, keep it square. Never round a corner.

rules.name: The Struck and Pale Rule
rules.body: A struck mark stands out from its field in full color. A pale mark sits one small step off its field, so it reads as not struck yet, but its letters still pass 4.5:1.

dos: Do start every hallmark row with the blued SP mark, then the standing, then Code.
Do give a new live product its own colorway: fill every role in the colorway table from its real colors, and check each text pair at 4.5:1 or better.
Do mark anything not built yet as pale, and give a pale layer the spoken label "not built yet".
Do use only real, public first screens of live products, taken from their own sites. Ship a phone capture for widths under 760px and a provenance file beside each image.
Do cut the corners of any standalone object with a bevel sized to it: 5px on marks, 7px on buttons, 8-12px on panels, rows and screens.
Do put the bevel on an inner face and the link outside it, so the 2px focus ring is never clipped.
Do keep every text control at least 44px tall.
Do set reading text in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next at 17px within the 46ch measure.
donts: Don't round a corner. border-radius stays 0.
Don't set text in capitals outside marks, and don't space out the letters of a heading.
Don't put a label, number or kicker above a section or page heading. The only thing above a page title is a back link.
Don't number page sections. Codes that belong to the content, like the exam's D1 to D5, go inside marks.
Don't add texture, grain, gradients or glass. Steel is a flat fill.
Don't draw hairline grids or divider rules between rows. Rows are separated by gaps and tone, and the only 1px lines are the screen frame and the masthead rule.
Don't lift anything but a product screen on a plate, and never use a hard offset shadow.
Don't recolor the SP mark, and don't let a product's colors leave its own plate, bench row, page header and share card.
Don't show the work as a grid of same-size cards or as text-left, image-right feature bands.
Don't use stock photos, illustrations, device mockups or invented screens. The headshot and real product screens are the only pictures.
Don't use text glyphs or icon fonts as icons, and don't put the diagonal arrow on a link that stays on the site or opens mail.
Don't hide a mark in order to animate it in. The strike presses a mark that is already there.
